proposed.explanation:
RANKING BY P/E (cheapest → most expensive):
1. ABUK: 76.21 / 11.65 (annualised 9M EPS) = 6.5×
2. EFID: 20.40 / 2.18 = 9.4×
3. TMGH: 82.50 / 6.98 = 11.8×
4. ETEL: 141.95 / 11.93 = 11.9×

RANKING BY EPS GROWTH (highest → lowest):
1. ETEL: +149 % (4.79 → 11.93) – but see data caveat below
2. ABUK: +104 % (4.28 → 8.74, 9M YoY)
3. EFID: +99 % (1.09 → 2.18)
4. TMGH: +59 % (4.38 → 6.98)

RANKING BY NET-PROFIT GROWTH:
1. EFID: +68 % (1.61 bn → 2.70 bn EGP)
2. TMGH: +43 % (12.77 bn → 18.20 bn EGP)
3. ABUK: no total-profit figure in the evidence (EPS only)
4. ETEL: −94 % (10.11 bn → 0.58 bn EGP) – contradicts its EPS rise; likely a one-off 2024 item or a data issue. Treat ETEL's growth picture as unreliable.

DATA CAVEAT – ETEL: The reported net profit fell from 10,111,328,000 EGP (FY24) to 578,063,000 EGP (FY25), yet EPS more than doubled (4.79 → 11.93). These two facts are mutually inconsistent unless the share count changed by ~97 %, which is implausible. I therefore discount ETEL's net-profit growth figure and rely only on its EPS for the P/E. This makes ETEL the least certain of the four.

ABUK AMBIGUOUS FIGURES: The 3-month-2026 EPS (printed as '199', likely 1.99) and both percentage-change columns could not be verified. I used only the verified 9-month EPS figures (8.74 and 4.28) and computed the 104 % growth myself. The 3-month acceleration/deceleration is therefore unknown.

SUGGESTED 4-STOCK ALLOCATION (100,000 EGP, equal-weight ≈ 25 % each):
• ABUK  328 sh × 76.21 = 24,997 EGP
• EFID 1,225 sh × 20.40 = 24,990 EGP
• TMGH  303 sh × 82.50 = 24,998 EGP
• ETEL  176 sh × 141.95 = 24,983 EGP
Total invested: 99,968 EGP; residual cash ≈ 32 EGP.

Why equal weight? All four P/Es sit in a narrow 6.5–11.9× band, all show positive EPS growth, and the investor has medium risk tolerance with a 7+ year horizon. Equal weighting avoids over-concentrating in any single name while the ETEL data issue and ABUK's 9-month-only record are resolved. No single holding exceeds 25 % of the portfolio, well within the 50 % cap.

RISKS: (1) ETEL's profit data is internally inconsistent – the stock may be cheaper or more expensive than it appears. (2) ABUK's 9-month annualisation assumes the final quarter matches the first three; a weak Q4 would raise the true P/E. (3) All four are Egyptian-listed; currency, regulatory, and macro risks apply. (4) Past growth does not guarantee future results. Revisit the allocation after ETEL's FY2026 report and ABUK's full-year 2026 results.
